record.original_question: The derived Torelli theorem for Enriques surfaces says that if X1 and X2 are smooth projective surfaces over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2, X1 is an Enriques surface, and Db(X1) is equivalent to Db(X2), then X1 is isomorphic to X2. Does this theorem remain true in characteristic 2 for some or all of the three characteristic-2 families of Enriques surfaces: classical, singular, and supersingular Enriques surfaces?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.4 (Derived Torelli theorem for Enriques surfaces). Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective surfaces defined over an algebraically closed field K of characteristic different from 2. If X1 is an Enriques surface and there is an exact equivalence Db (X1 ) = Db (X2 ), then X1 = X2.
But when char(K) = 2, then one gets three families: Classical Enriques surfaces ... Singular Enriques surfaces ... Supersingular Enriques surfaces ...
Question 2.5. Is Theorem 2.4 still true when char(K) = 2 for some/all of the three families above?

artifact.status_search_result: A 2016 note by Honigs-Lombardi-Tirabassi shows that the (twisted) derived category can distinguish the three families of Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2, but this does not establish the full derived Torelli statement. Subsequent refined derived Torelli results (Saccà–Macrì and others, 2019–2021) explicitly assume characteristic different from 2. No source found that proves or disproves derived Torelli for any of the three characteristic-2 families, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A note on the derived category of Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2
status_evidence.snippet: We show that the (twisted) derived category 'recognizes' the three different kinds of Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2
status_evidence.claim: Derived categories distinguish the three families, but full derived Torelli is not established.

status_evidence.title: A refined Derived Torelli Theorem for Enriques surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Refined derived Torelli for Enriques surfaces, assuming characteristic different from 2.
status_evidence.claim: Recent derived Torelli results explicitly exclude characteristic 2.

status_evidence.title: A refined derived Torelli theorem for Enriques surfaces, II
status_evidence.snippet: Non-generic case, again under the assumption char ≠ 2.
status_evidence.claim: Characteristic 2 case remains outside the scope of known results.
